entry.title: Bitcoin Core v30.5 Released
entry.summary:
Bitcoin Core version v30.5 introduces a range of bug fixes and performance enhancements, accompanied by updated translations to support a broader user base. The release is readily available for download at [https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-30.5/](https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-30.5/). Users are encouraged to report any issues encountered through the GitHub issue tracker at [https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues), ensuring ongoing improvements and community engagement.
Upgrading to this version involves shutting down any currently running instances of Bitcoin Core, waiting for a complete shutdown, and then proceeding with installation. Windows users should run the installer, while macOS users can copy over `/Applications/Bitcoin-Qt`, and Linux users should update the `bin/` and `libexec/` directories. Migration from end-of-life versions is supported, although it may require additional time if data directory updates are necessary. Backward compatibility with older wallet versions remains generally intact, promoting a smooth transition for existing users.
This version maintains robust compatibility across major operating systems, specifically those utilizing Linux Kernel 3.17+, macOS 13+, and Windows 10+. Although functionality on other Unix-like systems is typically present, these platforms do not receive the same level of testing, making their use less advisable for critical deployments.
Several notable technical changes are featured in this release. In networking, unique transaction inventory (INV) processing has been implemented to enhance efficiency. Continuous integration improvements include adopting pycapnp 2.2.1, switching to GitHub cache for all runners, streamlining runner selection, and integrating warp docker buildkit cache. These adjustments contribute to a more reliable and performant development and deployment workflow.
Acknowledgement is given to contributors such as fanquake, Greg Sanders, and willcl-ark, along with those who assisted with translation efforts, reflecting the collaborative nature of this project. For further announcements and participation, interested parties can join at [https://bitcoincore.org/en/list/announcements/join/](https://bitcoincore.org/en/list/announcements/join/).
